findings.title: Declared object permission check is missing on a return path
findings.description: A DRF view with an identifiable object-level policy returns lookup-derived data without an observed check on that object. This is bounded static evidence, not verified deployment exploitability.
findings.recommendation: Check the same requested object using the declared object-permission policy before exposing it.

obligation.required: Check the same requested object using the declared object-permission policy before exposing it.
obligation.observed: A DRF view with an identifiable object-level policy returns lookup-derived data without an observed check on that object.
assumptions: Queryset filtering, alternate checks and deployment reachability may affect actual exposure.

findings.title: JWT signature verification is explicitly disabled
findings.description: The resolved JWT decoder explicitly sets verify_signature=False. Application authentication use and runtime library behavior require validation.
findings.recommendation: Verify signatures using a fixed, compatible algorithm/key configuration; keep unverified decoding separate from trusted claims.

obligation.required: Bind signature verification to a trusted algorithm and compatible key.
obligation.observed: The resolved JWT decoder explicitly sets verify_signature=False.
assumptions: A decode/verify call is not itself proof that its claims are used for authentication.

findings.title: HTTP chunk footer is consumed without an observed byte check
findings.description: A resolved h11 receive-buffer read supplies footer bytes whose length advances a two-byte chunk delimiter state without an observed content check. This is bounded static evidence, not verified deployment exploitability.
findings.recommendation: Validate the exact CRLF footer, including fragmented prefixes, before advancing parser state.

obligation.required: Validate the exact CRLF footer, including fragmented prefixes, before advancing parser state.
obligation.observed: A resolved h11 receive-buffer read supplies footer bytes whose length advances a two-byte chunk delimiter state without an observed content check.
assumptions: The h11 receive-buffer and chunk-event contracts identify this as HTTP/1.1 chunk framing.

findings.title: Returned claims are parsed outside the verified JWS payload
findings.description: A keyed JWS deserialization accepts one payload representation, while returned claims are independently decoded from a compact-token segment. This is bounded static evidence, not verified deployment exploitability.
findings.recommendation: Return claims decoded from the verifier payload, or establish equality with that exact payload before returning them.

obligation.required: Return claims decoded from the verifier payload, or establish equality with that exact payload before returning them.
obligation.observed: A keyed JWS deserialization accepts one payload representation, while returned claims are independently decoded from a compact-token segment.
assumptions: The resolved jwcrypto JWS API may accept compact and JSON representations.
A non-null verification key, caller trust boundary and claim use remain runtime assumptions.

findings.title: HMAC key blacklist omits recognized public-key formats
findings.description: A finite public-key rejection list guards material stored for a resolved HMAC operation, but omits: -----BEGIN RSA PUBLIC KEY-----, -----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----, ssh-ed25519, ssh-dss, ecdsa-sha2-nistp256, ecdsa-sha2-nistp384, ecdsa-sha2-nistp521. This is bounded static evidence, not verified deployment exploitability.
findings.code_snippet:
if any(marker in key for marker in forbidden):
   raise ValueError()
findings.recommendation: Use a complete key-format/type boundary before accepting asymmetric representations as HMAC secrets.

obligation.required: Use a complete key-format/type boundary before accepting asymmetric representations as HMAC secrets.
obligation.observed: A finite public-key rejection list guards material stored for a resolved HMAC operation, but omits: -----BEGIN RSA PUBLIC KEY-----, -----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----, ssh-ed25519, ssh-dss, ecdsa-sha2-nistp256, ecdsa-sha2-nistp384, ecdsa-sha2-nistp521.
assumptions: This checks the visible finite blacklist, not all possible key-format parsers or caller restrictions.
Accepting omitted representations and an attacker-relevant verifier configuration require runtime validation.

findings.title: HTTP framing length uses permissive integer parsing
findings.description: A resolved HTTP parser converts a Content-Length or chunk-size value without an observed lexical rejection guard. Python integer conversion accepts extra forms. This is bounded static evidence, not verified deployment exploitability.
findings.recommendation: Validate the exact decimal or hexadecimal HTTP length grammar before integer conversion; reject signs, prefixes and whitespace.

obligation.required: Validate the exact decimal or hexadecimal HTTP length grammar before integer conversion; reject signs, prefixes and whitespace.
obligation.observed: A resolved HTTP parser converts a Content-Length or chunk-size value without an observed lexical rejection guard. Python integer conversion accepts extra forms.
assumptions: Only visible dominating guards and resolved HTTP library contracts are modelled; caller filtering remains unverified.
Recognizing a lexical guard does not certify its regular expression or all parser paths.

findings.title: Unsupported transfer codings have no rejecting branch
findings.description: The HTTP parser handles only the chunked value in its Transfer-Encoding branch and has no alternate rejection in that branch. This is bounded static evidence, not verified deployment exploitability.
findings.recommendation: Reject unsupported Transfer-Encoding values before choosing a request body reader.

obligation.required: Reject unsupported Transfer-Encoding values before choosing a request body reader.
obligation.observed: The HTTP parser handles only the chunked value in its Transfer-Encoding branch and has no alternate rejection in that branch.
assumptions: This is a narrow branch-shape check, not a complete HTTP framing, proxy or deployment model.
